text.p: Pakistan's caretaker government re-arrested ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto's husband on Wednesday immediately after withdrawing an earlier detention order challenged in a court, a spokesman for her party said.

He said Asif Ali Zardari, investment minister in Bhutto's cabinet, was picked up from a government resthouse near Islamabad where he had been kept for three weeks since President Farooq Leghari dismissed her administration.

Zardari was taken to his home province of Sindh under a new detention order, the spokesman said. A police official in Karachi, capital of Sindh, said he was flown into the city escorted by federal investigators and handed over to the Karachi police's crime branch.
The official said he was being held under the Maintenance of Public Order ordinance. He refused to say where Zardari was being kept.
The official said formal charges might be brought against him by the Sindh provincial government on Thursday but refused to give details.
Earlier the Lahore High Court had cancelled a petition from Bhutto challenging Zardari's detention, after a government lawyer told it the detention order had been withdrawn.
Zardari was served with another detention order from the Sindh provincial government before he could be released, the spokesman for Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) said.
No reason was given in the order, he said, calling it "the law of jungle".

No charges have been brought against Zardari, leading Bhutto to go to the Lahore High Court to challenge his detention. He has been held since November 5, when Leghari dismissed Bhutto's government on charges of corruption and misrule, which she denies.

The caretaker government led by Prime Minister Meraj Khalid at first said Zardari, kept incommunicado for 48 hours, was being held in protective custody. Later it cited the Maintenance of Public Order ordinance to justify his detention.
On Tuesday, Bhutto and her three children met Zardari at the resthouse near Islamabad.
In 1994, Zardari was cleared of the last of 13 similar charges brought against him after the first Bhutto government was dismissed by presidential order four years earlier.
